facts.content: Patient has a 3-day worsening headache.
Headache is holocephalic, predominantly right peri-orbital, dull with intermittent sharp spikes.
facts.source_text: Holocephalic, predominately R peri-orbital; dull with intermittent sharp spikes

facts.content: Headache is constant with fluctuating intensity and pain is rated 8/10.
Patient experiences photophobia and brief 'shooting lights' at onset.
Patient has nausea with the headache but no vomiting.
The headache is not associated with visual loss, speech difficulty, focal weakness, neck stiffness, head injury, fever, or rash.
facts.source_text: No visual loss/blurring, no speech difficulty, no focal weakness, no neck stiffness, no head injury, no fever, no rash

facts.content: Potential triggers for the headache include screen use, mild work stress, and possibly hydration.
facts.source_text: Trigger concerns: screen use; mild work stress; hydration considered

facts.content: The headache has impacted concentration, caused the patient to be off work for 2 days, and led to reduced screen brightness.
facts.source_text: Impact: ↓ concentration; off work x2 days; reduced screen brightness

facts.content: No past medical history reported.
Patient has taken ibuprofen a few tablets daily for 2 days, approximately 3 per day.
facts.source_text: Meds: Ibuprofen “a few” tabs daily x2 days; ~3/day

facts.content: No regular medications taken.
No known drug allergies reported.
Mother and sister have migraines, with mother's being frequent and seasonal.
facts.source_text: Mother and sister with migraines (mother frequent, seasonal)

facts.content: Patient lives with 3 housemates and works in IT with heavy computer use.
facts.source_text: Lives with 3 housemates; works in IT (heavy computer use)

facts.content: Patient socially smokes and drinks socially.
Patient wears glasses since childhood and has not recently had an eye test.
facts.source_text: Wears glasses since childhood; no recent eye test

facts.content: Acute headache is likely migraine-type.
Poor response to low-dose or under-dosed ibuprofen.
Strong family history of migraine.
No red flags: afebrile, no neck stiffness, focal deficits, speech changes, or trauma.
facts.source_text: No red flags: afebrile, no neck stiffness, focal deficits, speech changes, or trauma

facts.content: Optimize ibuprofen dosing up to 2 tablets three times a day.
facts.source_text: Optimize ibuprofen dosing (up to 2 tabs TID as discussed)

facts.content: Prescribe stronger NSAID like naproxen if needed.
Consider add-on analgesics such as paracetamol or codeine.
facts.source_text: Consider add-on analgesics: paracetamol or codeine

facts.content: Advise keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.
Advise screen hygiene including breaks and brightness adjustments.
Consider optometry review if eye strain persists.
facts.source_text: Consider optometry review if eye strain persists

facts.content: Review in 1–2 weeks.
If headaches become frequent, discuss prophylaxis options.
facts.source_text: If headaches become frequent, discuss prophylaxis options

facts.content: Return to ED or doctor if headaches worsen, or if there are visual changes, focal weakness/numbness, speech difficulty, fever, neck stiffness, or if generally unwell.
facts.source_text: Return/ED for worsening headache, visual changes, focal weakness/numbness, speech difficulty, fever, neck stiffness, or if generally unwell
